source: Producer shares per resource, each with its own source below: oil — US EIA International Energy Statistics 2025 crude + condensate (as reported by Enerdata, Shafaq/EIA and Rigzone/Energy Institute, 2026); gas — Energy Institute Statistical Review of World Energy 2025 (2024 data, world 4,124.5 bcm); rare earths — IEA Global Critical Minerals Outlook 2024 refining shares (China ≈ 90 % of separation) with USGS Mineral Commodity Summaries 2026 mine output for context; advanced semiconductors — TrendForce (May 2024) foundry capacity at 16/14 nm and below, 2024; food — FAOSTAT cereal production 2023 (rounded) ; steel — worldsteel crude steel production 2025 (world 1,848.9 Mt; China 960.8, India 164.9, Japan 80.7) via Expometals. World trade values are order-of-magnitude game estimates (volume × typical 2024–25 price). Demand weights are a game model, not data.
notes: Shares are fractions of world production (1.0 = world). Entries with "estimate": true in a resource's estimatedProducers list are rounded approximations from the named source family or public reporting, not exact figures. The remainder (1 − Σ listed) is diffuse production by many small producers, available to every importer whose shipping is not blockaded. demandGdpWeight: share of each nation's demand that scales with its GDP (the rest scales with population). gdpWeight: percentage points of annual growth lost at a 100 % shortage. seizedYield: share of a capitulated nation's capacity its conqueror can run (fabs need foreign tools and staff, so chips are nearly worthless when seized).

resources.name: Crude oil
resources.description: Fuel for economies and armies. Tanks, ships and aircraft burn it; importers pay the bill when supply tightens.
resources.source: US EIA 2025: United States 13.6 mb/d (16 % of world), Russia 9.9, Saudi Arabia 9.5, Canada 5.0, Iraq 4.4, China 4.3, Brazil 3.8, Iran 3.1, UAE 3.1, Kuwait 2.6; world crude + condensate ≈ 82 mb/d. Smaller producers rounded from EIA country briefs.

resources.name: Natural gas
resources.description: Heats homes, powers grids and feeds fertiliser and chemical plants. Pipeline and LNG flows are hard to replace quickly.
resources.source: Energy Institute Statistical Review 2025 (2024 data): world 4,124.5 bcm; United States 1,033 bcm, Russia 629.9, Iran 262.9; Qatar ≈ 179.5; others rounded from the same review.

resources.name: Rare earths
resources.description: Separated rare-earth oxides for permanent magnets in motors, missiles, radars and drones. Mining is spread out; refining is concentrated in China.
resources.source: IEA Global Critical Minerals Outlook 2024: China ≈ 90 % of rare-earth refining. USGS Mineral Commodity Summaries 2026 (mine output 2025e, world 390 kt): China 270 kt, United States 51 kt, Australia 29 kt, Burma 22 kt, Thailand 4.8 kt. Non-Chinese refining shares (Lynas in Malaysia, US, Vietnam, Estonia) are rounded estimates.

resources.name: Advanced semiconductors
resources.description: Leading-edge logic (16/14 nm and below) for AI, aircraft, guided weapons and data centres. Most of it is made in Taiwan.
resources.source: TrendForce, May 2024: share of foundry capacity at 16/14 nm and below in 2024 — Taiwan 66 %, South Korea 11 %, United States 10 %, China 9 %. The remaining ~4 % (Japan, Israel, Ireland, Singapore) is split as an estimate.

resources.name: Food (cereals)
resources.description: Staple grains. A shortage raises prices, cuts stability and brings people into the streets.
resources.source: FAOSTAT cereal production 2023 (world ≈ 2.85 Gt), rounded shares; Russia, Ukraine, the EU, Canada and Australia lead wheat exports (USDA 2024/25: Russia ≈ 44 Mt, EU ≈ 27 Mt, Canada ≈ 26 Mt, Australia ≈ 25 Mt).

resources.name: Steel
resources.description: Hulls, armour, shells and factories. War economies devour it.
resources.source: worldsteel 2025 crude steel production via Expometals: world 1,848.9 Mt; China 960.8, India 164.9, Japan 80.7. Others rounded from worldsteel's 2025 monthly releases.

unitInputs.source: Game design: which strategic inputs each unit type and research branch consumes (weights sum to 1).
